note: Distinct from B1/B2's consumer-facing media-literacy vocabulary (Falschmeldung, Filterblase, Algorithmus): this unit's vocabulary examines journalism as a craft and institution, and how it shapes what audiences see.

examples.de: Medienkritik untersucht, wie Medien Themen auswählen und darstellen.
examples.en: Media criticism examines how media select and present topics.

note: The right of the press to report without state control or censorship — a constitutionally protected principle in Germany.

examples.de: Die Pressefreiheit ist in Artikel 5 des Grundgesetzes verankert.
examples.en: Freedom of the press is enshrined in Article 5 of the Basic Law.

note: A common description of the press's role alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary — checking power rather than holding it.

examples.de: Die Presse wird oft als vierte Gewalt neben Legislative, Exekutive und Judikative bezeichnet.
examples.en: The press is often called the fourth estate alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary.

note: The group of journalists and editors who decide what a publication covers and how.

examples.de: Die Redaktion entscheidet, welche Themen in die Zeitung kommen.
examples.en: The editorial team decides which topics make it into the paper.

note: The person with final responsibility for a publication's content.

examples.de: Der Chefredakteur trägt die Verantwortung für den gesamten Inhalt.
examples.en: The editor-in-chief bears responsibility for the entire content.

note: Radio and television broadcasting collectively — der öffentlich-rechtliche Rundfunk, der Rundfunkbeitrag.

examples.de: Der Rundfunk umfasst sowohl Radio als auch Fernsehen.
examples.en: Broadcasting includes both radio and television.

note: Describes broadcasters funded by public fees rather than advertising or subscriptions — öffentlich-rechtliche Sender, in contrast to private commercial channels.

examples.de: Öffentlich-rechtliche Sender finanzieren sich hauptsächlich über Gebühren.
examples.en: Public broadcasters finance themselves mainly through fees.

note: The investigative legwork behind a news story — a journalist's Recherche, distinct from B2's academic Forschung.

examples.de: Eine gründliche Recherche ist die Grundlage jedes seriösen Artikels.
examples.en: Thorough research is the foundation of any serious article.

note: Journalism that actively digs up hidden wrongdoing, rather than reporting on events as they happen. No natural plural.

examples.de: Investigativjournalismus deckt Missstände auf, die sonst verborgen blieben.
examples.en: Investigative journalism uncovers wrongdoing that would otherwise stay hidden.

note: A piece where the publication states its own position openly, unlike a neutral news report.

examples.de: Im Leitartikel bezieht die Zeitung offen Stellung.
examples.en: In the editorial, the newspaper openly states its position.

note: The large title meant to draw a reader in — quality and reißerisch headlines aim at very different effects.

examples.de: Eine reißerische Schlagzeile soll vor allem Klicks bringen.
examples.en: A sensationalist headline is meant above all to generate clicks.

note: An official statement an organisation issues to the press, often the starting point for a story rather than the whole of it.

examples.de: Die Firma reagierte mit einer knappen Pressemitteilung.
examples.en: The company responded with a brief press release.

note: A person who provides a journalist with information, often confidentially — journalists have strong legal protections for keeping an Informant's identity secret.

examples.de: Journalisten müssen ihre Informanten oft schützen.
examples.en: Journalists often have to protect their informants.

note: Presenting the same facts within a particular interpretive frame, shaping how an audience understands a topic without changing the facts themselves. No natural plural.

examples.de: Framing beeinflusst, wie ein Thema wahrgenommen wird, ohne dass Fakten verändert werden.
examples.en: Framing influences how a topic is perceived, without the facts themselves being changed.

note: The media's power to determine which topics the public thinks and talks about, regardless of what position is taken on them. No natural plural.

examples.de: Durch Agenda-Setting bestimmen Medien mit, worüber die Öffentlichkeit überhaupt nachdenkt.
examples.en: Through agenda-setting, media help determine what the public thinks about at all.

note: Presenting an event as a scandal, often out of proportion to its actual significance. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Skandalisierung einzelner Fälle verzerrt oft das Gesamtbild.
examples.en: The sensationalising of individual cases often distorts the overall picture.

note: Describes coverage designed to shock or grab attention rather than inform accurately — ein reißerischer Titel.

examples.de: Ein reißerischer Titel verspricht oft mehr, als der Artikel hält.
examples.en: A sensationalist title often promises more than the article delivers.

note: Journalism that favours emotional, personal, or sensational stories over careful analysis — the opposite end of the spectrum from Qualitätsjournalismus. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Boulevardjournalismus setzt stärker auf Emotionen als auf Fakten.
examples.en: Tabloid journalism relies more heavily on emotions than on facts.

note: Journalism marked by careful research, verification, and balance — the counterpart to Boulevardjournalismus. No natural plural.

examples.de: Qualitätsjournalismus zeichnet sich durch sorgfältige Recherche aus.
examples.en: Quality journalism is characterised by careful research.

note: The professional expectation that reporting presents multiple sides fairly, rather than pushing one view. No natural plural.

examples.de: Das Objektivitätsgebot verlangt, mehrere Perspektiven fair darzustellen.
examples.en: The objectivity requirement demands presenting multiple perspectives fairly.

note: A formal set of ethical standards journalists and publications commit to follow. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Pressekodex legt ethische Standards für Journalisten fest.
examples.en: The press code sets ethical standards for journalists.

note: A headline or teaser designed to generate clicks through exaggerated or misleading promises.

examples.de: Klickköder locken mit übertriebenen Versprechen, die der Inhalt nicht einlöst.
examples.en: Clickbait lures with exaggerated promises the content doesn't deliver on.

note: A barrier requiring payment or subscription before a reader can access an article.

examples.de: Viele Zeitungen setzen inzwischen auf eine Paywall.
examples.en: Many newspapers now rely on a paywall.

note: The overall range and mix of media outlets in a country — often discussed in terms of how concentrated or diverse it is. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die deutsche Medienlandschaft ist vielfältig, aber zunehmend konzentriert.
examples.en: The German media landscape is diverse, but increasingly concentrated.

note: Close to Investigativjournalismus — journalism specifically aimed at bringing a hidden wrongdoing into public view. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Enthüllungsjournalismus brachte den Skandal erst ans Licht.
examples.en: Exposé journalism was what first brought the scandal to light.

note: A story only one outlet has, usually obtained through an Informant or original Recherche.

examples.de: Die Zeitung veröffentlichte einen Exklusivbericht über den Fall.
examples.en: The paper published an exclusive report on the case.

note: How many people a piece of media actually reaches — a measure of distribution, not of quality or accuracy.

examples.de: Die Reichweite eines Beitrags sagt nichts über seine Qualität aus.
examples.en: A piece's reach says nothing about its quality.

note: Deliberately false or misleading information spread on purpose — distinct from B1's Falschmeldung, which can also arise from simple error.

examples.de: Desinformation wird gezielt eingesetzt, um Meinungen zu manipulieren.
examples.en: Disinformation is deliberately used to manipulate opinions.
